Content standard: B1.2.3.1. Demonstrate understanding of why Ghana used to be called the ‘Gold Coast’.
Indicator wording: Recall when the name Ghana came into formal use.
Source notes: Printed page 5 asks for the year of the name change without giving its date. Date-reading exercises supply an independence label or refer to the class timeline.

Content standard: B1.2.5.1. Show understanding of significant roles played by Ghanaians from different walks of life
Indicator wording: Identify Ghanaians of diverse fields who have contributed significantly to national development including Theodosia Okoh – National flag. Amon Kotei – Coat of Arms. Baba Yara – Football for Ghana. Ephraim Amu – Music, Kofi Antubam – Art and craft, Kow Ansah – Film etc.

Content standard: B1.3.1.1 Show understanding of Europeans who came to Ghana
Indicator wording: Explore which Europeans came to Ghana

Content standard: B1.6.1.1. Demonstrate understanding of the presidents that have ruled Ghana since 1960
Indicator wording: Identify the Presidents Ghana has had since 1960
Source notes: Printed page 8 sets a 1960–2016 enquiry and calls for a labelled class gallery. It does not supply the portraits or list the officeholders and tenures. Name and tenure performances use a teacher-provided album.

Content standard: B2.2.1.1. Demonstrate knowledge of the ethnic groups in Ghana
Indicator wording: Identify the ethnic groups in each region in Ghana
Source notes: Printed page 10 gives the same indicator code to the region-matching and characteristics objectives. The curriculum does not list regional matches or dates of creation. Map exercises give their own keys and do not score an unsupported sequence of regions.

Content standard: B2.2.1.1. Show understanding of the characteristics of some of the ethnic groups in Ghana
Indicator wording: State the characteristics of the ethnic groups in Ghana
Source notes: Printed page 10 repeats the preceding indicator code for this separate objective. Printed page 10 gives categories of cultural characteristics but no named festival accounts. Tasks provide descriptions or invite a teacher-checked local example.

Content standard: B2.2.4.1. Exhibit knowledge of the history of the major historical locations in Ghana
Indicator wording: Discuss the history of Ghana’s major historical locations. Examples include Kumasi military museum, Komfo Anokye Sword, Assin Manso slave site, Gbewa Palace.
Source notes: The class section names sites but does not give dates or a sequence by age. Activities use brief guide accounts and ask children to identify what those accounts show.

Content standard: B2.2.5.1.1 Exhibit understanding of Ghanaian women who have contributed significantly to Ghana’s development
Indicator wording: Identify Ghanaian women who have made significant contributions to national development
Source notes: Printed page 12 uses B2.2.5.1.1 in its content-standard column and places a full stop after the same code in the indicator column.

Content standard: B2.3.2.1. Understand that trade was the major reason why the Europeans settled in Ghana
Indicator wording: Describe how early trade was carried out between Ghanaians and Europeans
Source notes: Printed page 13 lists trade goods together without consistently identifying their direction. The questions specify who gives each item in illustrative exchanges.

Content standard: B3.2.1.1. Exhibit knowledge of the unique history of the major ethnic groups in Ghana
Indicator wording: Discuss the origins of the major ethnic groups in Ghana
Source notes: The exemplar names ethnic groups and asks pupils to trace migration routes, but supplies no named places of origin, migration dates or routes. Illustrative maps and travel accounts in the questions are fictional.

Content standard: B3 2.2.1. Demonstrate knowledge of how intergroup alliances, conflicts and other exchanges
Indicator wording: Discuss the nature of exchanges among the ethnic groups.
Source notes: The printed code has a space after B3. The standard ends with “exchanges” in the table.

Content standard: B3 2.2.1. Demonstrate knowledge of how intergroup alliances, conflicts and other exchanges
Indicator wording: Name some of the items exchanged among the various groups.
Source notes: The standard appears incomplete. The enquiry asks about the origin of cedi but gives no full derivation.

Content standard: B3 2.2.1. Demonstrate knowledge of how intergroup alliances, conflicts and other exchanges
Indicator wording: Describe the conflicts and alliances that existed among the ethnic groups in Ghana
Source notes: The end of the Akatamanso and Ada War exemplar runs together. Only clearly attached dates and parties are assessed.

Content standard: B3.2.4.1. Demonstrate knowledge of the forts and castle built in Ghana.
Indicator wording: Identify the forts and castles built along the coast of Ghana
Source notes: This page lists uses and investigation activities without supplying named sites, builders, towns or construction dates. No site-specific matches are asserted.

Content standard: B3.2.5.1. Describe the contributions of some outstanding Ghanaian entrepreneurs.
Indicator wording: Describe Ghanaian entrepreneurs who have made significant contributions including George Grant – Businessman, Winifred Tete-Ansa, Esther Ocloo – Nkulenu Industries, B.A. Mensah – Pioneer Tobacco Ltd. Kwabena Pepra – Paramount Distilleries, J.K. Siaw – Tata Brewery, Alhaji Adam Iddrisu - Global Haulage
Source notes: The exemplar supplies names and enterprise associations, but no full biographical accounts.

Content standard: B3.3.1.1. Show understanding of the interactions between the local people and early settlers
Indicator wording: Describe how the Europeans settled on the Gold Coast, including forming alliances with the local chiefs
Source notes: The meeting is named without a transcript. Classroom dialogues are expressly fictional.

Content standard: B4.1.4.1. Demonstrate knowledge of the history of some historical locations in Ghana
Indicator wording: Describe the history of Ghana’s major historical locations, specifically, Flagstaff house, Burma camp, James Town light house, Gbewa Palace, Larabanga Mosque etc.
Source notes: The printed code begins B4.1 although the table is in Strand 2. Builder names and construction dates are not supplied.

Content standard: B4.2.5.1. Demonstrate understanding of the role of significant traditional rulers in Ghana’s history
Indicator wording: Identify the role played by some traditional rulers in the national development including Dode Akaibi of Accra, Ndewura Jakpa of Gonja, Osei Tutu I of Asante, Gbewaa of Pusiga, Togbe Sri I., Sir Ofori Atta of Akim Abuakwa, Nana Kobina Nketsia I of Esikado etc.
Source notes: The excerpt names rulers and several associated communities without supplying a biography for each ruler.

Content standard: B4.3.3.1. Demonstrate knowledge of Europeans’ engagement in other activities other than trade in Ghana
Indicator wording: Describe European missionary activities in Ghana
Source notes: The two society-place examples do not provide a full chronological list of missionaries.

Strand: Colonisation and Developments under Colonial Rule in Ghana

Indicator wording: Examine the Bond of 1844
Source notes: The indicator and enquiry repeatedly identify 1844. One exemplar says “content of 1884”. Neither the text of the Bond nor a list of signatories is reproduced.

Strand: Colonisation and Developments under Colonial Rule in Ghana

Indicator wording: Describe how the different areas – The Colony, Asante, The Northern Territories and The British Mandated Togoland– became one territory known as the Gold Coast
Source notes: The page lists the areas, a role-play and a map comparison. It does not reproduce the agreements or a full sequence of dates.

Content standard: B4.6.1.1. Understand that there have been four Republics in Ghana
Indicator wording: Explain that Ghana up to June 1960, though independent, had the Queen of The United Kingdom (UK) as Head of State of the Ghana and made limitations on Ghana’s independence.

Content standard: B4.6.1.1. Understand that there have been four Republics in Ghana
Indicator wording: State the dates and names of the leaders of the four Republics of Ghana since 1960
